row.notes: In Game_PitLane_UpdateMovement's InPitBox step, after the hold seconds are chosen: xmm0 = g_stopGoDuration (0x145f9677c) when Sess_Penalty_IsServedAtNextStop (call 0x1434b9fc8, edx = r12d) answered true, else 0. r12d = vehicle, r14 = the car's pit lane movement record (+0xe4 box clock, +0xe8 crew job time, +0xf8 feature-flag box clock), rsi = movement manager. Nothing writes xmm0 before the two release compares (0x1434ba0b7: box clock > crew time + xmm0; 0x1434ba6c8 flag path: +0xf8 >= xmm0 + setting), so adding seconds to xmm0 here holds that car longer. On the non-flag path the compare at 0x1434ba0b7 runs only when the car's crew entry (r9) is found; with none the car is released at 0x1434ba0c5 and added seconds do nothing.

verify.notes: gh:serve-verify Confirmed in Game_PitLane_UpdateMovement state 4 (table at 0x1434b88a0): r14 = [[rsp+0x60]], the record of vehicle r12d (0x1434b8993), not rewritten on the paths to the site; al = Sess_Penalty_IsServedAtNextStop(edx=r12d) from 0x1434b9fc8; xmm0 = 0 (0x1434ba031, jmp 0x1434ba035 to the site) or [0x145f9677c] (0x1434ba037). The site is the join point and no branch lands inside its 7 bytes. xmm0 is not written before 0x1434ba0b7 (release when +0xe4 > +0xe8 + xmm0) or 0x1434ba6c8 (release when +0xf8 >= xmm0 + setting); every branch into those compares comes from after the site. Difference: on the non-flag path the compare runs only when a crew entry r9 is found; r9 = 0 releases the car at 0x1434ba0c5 without it. Same shape on 1.0.145 at 0x1434bc5bf.
